title: Expression écrite — to template
objective: Make the shape of each writing task automatic so working memory goes to content. Four marked pieces.
tasks: Write each template out five times until it needs no thought
Four marked pieces (at least one of each tâche)
Fold in past-participle agreement with a preceding direct object (deferred from week 4)

steps.title: Templates aren't cheating
steps.body:
They're **cognitive offloading**: if the shape is automatic, working memory goes to content. Write each out five times, then only content varies.
Writing = 60 minutes for all three tâches.

steps.title: Tâche 1 — informal message (~60–120 words, tu)
steps.body:
**Greeting** → **why you're writing** → **two or three details** → **a question to the reader** → **sign-off**.
*Salut Léa ! Je t'écris parce que … D'abord … Ensuite … Et toi, tu … ? Bises, …*
**Simple tenses done accurately beat ambitious ones done badly.**

steps.title: Tâche 2 — semi-formal recount + opinion (~120–150)
steps.body:
**Context** → **what happened (PC/imparfait)** → **your reaction** → **opinion with one reason and one example** → **close**.
This is where PC/imparfait is graded hardest — why month II mattered.

steps.title: Tâche 3 — compare two opposing texts (~120–180)
steps.body:
**Text A's position** → **text B's** → **where they clash** → **your position with two arguments** → **nuanced conclusion**.
***Never just summarise*** — you're marked on the comparison and on having a stance.
*Selon le premier document … Le second, au contraire, … Les deux textes s'opposent sur … Pour ma part, … En somme, …*

steps.q: Tâche 3: what's the most common way to lose marks?
options: Summarising both texts without taking a stance

steps.title: Now fold in: agreement with a preceding direct object
steps.body:
With **avoir**, the participle agrees with a direct object that comes **before** it:
*les lettres que j'ai écrit**es*** · *Ta sœur ? Je l'ai vu**e**.*
Cheap now, and examiners see it in writing.

steps.q: *Les documents que j'ai ___ sont sur la table.*

steps.title: Tâche 1 — timed 10 minutes
steps.task: Write to a friend who is visiting you next month: tell them what you'll do together and ask what they'd like to eat.
steps.prompt: Votre ami(e) vient vous rendre visite le mois prochain. Écrivez-lui un message (60–120 mots).

steps.title: Tâche 2 — timed 20 minutes
steps.task: Article for a community blog: tell about a volunteering experience and give your opinion on volunteering.
steps.prompt: Racontez une expérience de bénévolat pour le blog de votre quartier et donnez votre opinion (120–150 mots).

steps.title: Tâche 3 — timed 30 minutes
steps.task: Doc 1: *Les écrans aident les enfants à apprendre : applications éducatives, accès à l'information, préparation au monde numérique.* Doc 2: *Les écrans nuisent aux enfants : troubles du sommeil, manque d'activité physique, baisse de la concentration.* Compare, then give your position.
steps.prompt: Les écrans et les enfants : comparez les deux points de vue et donnez votre opinion (120–180 mots).

points: T1: greeting → why → details → question → sign-off
T2: context → story (PC/imp) → reaction → opinion + reason + example → close
T3: A → B → clash → your stance + 2 arguments → nuanced conclusion. Never just summarise

items.q: Bien que ce ___ cher, c'est utile.
Selon le premier texte, …; le second, ___ , …
